name: A.N.R. Robinson International Airport
before:
Tobago's airport, at Crown Point in the south west of the island, 11 km from the capital Scarborough. It is one of two international airports in Trinidad and Tobago, the other being Piarco on Trinidad.

There are two terminals and the split is not the usual one. The International Terminal handles international traffic, cargo, general aviation and helicopters, with seven parking positions. The Regional or North Terminal is the main passenger building and takes everything to and from Trinidad and the rest of the Caribbean, with six positions. Most clients arriving from a Caribbean hub will use the regional building, not the international one.

An expansion programme has been running since February 2004. The instrument landing system, the new domestic terminal and the air traffic control modernisation are complete, while a new control tower and a landside transit mall were still pending.

It was formerly Crown Point International, so both names appear in supplier systems.
after:
Tobago's airport, 11 km from the capital, Scarborough. It is one of two international airports in Trinidad and Tobago, the other being Piarco on Trinidad.

The airports authority said in September 2025 that a new terminal was in its final stages, with airside works still under way. In its budget that October, the government said the airport would be fully operational by mid-2026. Check which terminal a client will use.

It was formerly Crown Point International, so both names appear in supplier systems.

claims.inAfter: The airports authority said in September 2025 that a new terminal was in its final stages, with airside works still under way.
claims.note: Attributed statement, checked against the authority's own release of 22 September 2025 (a year and a day old, so it is dated in the text). It also says the handover from NIDCO, the project manager, to the authority was under way and that the terminal would be commissioned 'at the earliest possible time'. Wikipedia's 'slated for completion in February 2025' was overtaken.

claims.claim: government budget, October 2025: airport fully operational by mid-2026
claims.inAfter: In its budget that October, the government said the airport would be fully operational by mid-2026.
claims.note: Attributed statement, checked against the Budget Statement 2026 (13 October 2025). Its words are 'by the second quarter of Fiscal 2026'; the statement does not define its fiscal year, and 'by mid-2026' holds whether that quarter is January to March or April to June 2026. Nothing from 2026 was found to say whether the terminal has opened: the authority's releases since September 2025 and Caribbean Airlines' releases from October 2025 to September 2026 carry no notice of a terminal move at Tobago; the Tobago House of Assembly site refused the connection and Newsday answered 502. Hence the advice to check.
